subject: DPA bridging runbook — UK Addendum / TIA sequencing & evidence handoff
messages:
From: Michael Shears <michael.shears@aureliahealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: legal@aureliahealth.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Data transfer evidence & sequencing for UK addendum (TIA scope)

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement checklist we need to lock the transfer safeguards (SCCs + UK Addendum) and the Technical/Organisational measures (TIA/DTIA) sequencing before legal signs the DPA.

Can you confirm:
- What evidence you can provide that maps to the TIA control families (logging, encryption in transit/at rest, KMS, access controls, subprocessor list + attestation chronology).
- Whether Redwood will sign the UK Addendum or provide equivalent contractual commitments for our UK operations.
- A proposed timeline for the evidence handoff (we need items packaged by next Friday).

Attached is a simple tracker we use (Aurelia_TIA_Request.xlsx) showing the controls we expect mapped to evidence artifacts.

Also copying Aurelia Legal for visibility — they may request narrow redlines to the proposed UK Addendum.

Appreciate a quick plan you can share so legal can calendar their review.

Best,
Michael
Director, Procurement — Aurelia Health

Attachment: Aurelia_TIA_Request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Shears <michael.shears@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer evidence & sequencing for UK addendum (TIA scope)

Michael —

Thanks for the tracker and the clear ask. Draft plan below, plus proposed owners. I kept the sequencing tight to meet your calendar.

Summary plan (high level):
1) UK Addendum position: Redwood will sign the standard UK Addendum (we already include UK Addendum in enterprise DPAs). We can provide an annotated copy if Aurelia Legal needs clarifications. Owner: me.

2) Evidence mapping to TIA control families:
   - Encryption: certs + KMS key policy snippets + encryption-at-rest architecture diagram. Owner: Jonas.
   - Logging & audit: sample audit logs (redacted), retention policy, SIEM ingest diagram. Owner: Logan.
   - Access controls & IAM: RBAC matrix export, onboarding/offboarding runbook. Owner: Jonas.
   - Subprocessor chronology: current subprocessor CSV + signed attestation from critical subprocessors (where possible). Owner: Laura (legal coordination).

3) Packaging & delivery cadence:
   - Day 1 (Tue): provide the annotated UK Addendum + high-level DPA clause mapping doc.
   - Day 2-3: evidence artifacts (encryption, IAM, logging) uploaded to shared Drive folder.
   - Day 4: subprocessor list + attestation inventory.
   - Day 5 (Fri): consolidated evidence pack and short Q&A call (30 min).

We will put attachments in a shared folder and supply a single index PDF (Redwood_UKAddendum_Checklist_v1.pdf) that maps Aurelia rows to artifacts. If Aurelia Legal prefers a DocuSign path for the UK Addendum we can prepare that after redline resolution.

Open questions / decisions we need from Aurelia:
- Do you require escrowed logs or additional retention beyond our standard 13 months?
- Any IP/processing carveouts for UK operations that would change subprocessor exposure?

I can run the Q&A on Friday. Jonas and Logan are copied to own the technical artifacts.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_UKAddendum_Checklist_v1.pdf (index)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Michael Shears <michael.shears@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer evidence & sequencing for UK addendum (TIA scope)

Thanks Laura. A couple of technical clarifications from our side before we package:

- KMS: we use customer-controlled keys for Private deployments; for Hosted/Dedicated we use AWS KMS with CMKs managed by Redwood. I will include the Key Policy export and a short note on key rotation cadence.

- Logging: sample SIEM export will be redacted to remove customer PII; retention default is 13 months (we can support a 24-month exception via addendum but that will need procurement approval).

- Subprocessors: we can provide signed attestation letters from critical GPU infra providers and from our logging provider; for smaller subprocessors we provide contractual commitments and CSV history. Expect the attestation artifacts on Day 4.

One more ask — can Aurelia confirm the jurisdictional scope (UK only vs UK + EU) so I can include sequence notes for SCCs vs UK Addendum? If you expect EU processing we will additionally map the EU SCCs artifacts and note cross-border handoff points.

jonas
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Laura / Jonas / Logan —

Thanks, that plan looks good and aligns with our procurement timeline. A couple quick answers:

- Jurisdictional scope: UK-only for now; we will request EU mapping later if the pilot expands.
- Retention: 13 months is fine for initial procurement. If we move to production we may revisit 24-months.

We confirm the Q&A call Friday at 11:00am BST (I booked a calendar hold and sent an invite to the Redwood team). Please upload artifacts to the Drive link you shared and ping when the index PDF is ready.

One small redline note from legal: they will want a clause clarifying that subprocessor attestation is provided within 15 business days of request for critical subprocessors. They asked me to flag it now so we can identify any blocking subprocessors early.

Michael
Director, Procurement — Aurelia Health
